find:
IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM updater.plans p WHERE p.plan_id = NEW.plan_id
      AND p.state = 'approved' AND p.expires_at > pg_catalog.now()) THEN
why: B2: a run must be bound to an approved, unexpired plan at INSERT, or a refused or expired approval can still start an update. Removing the check lets an INSERT against a closed plan through.

find:
IF NEW.state = 'superseded' AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM updater.runs r WHERE r.plan_id = OLD.plan_id AND r.finished_at IS NULL) THEN
replace:
IF NEW.state = 'superseded' AND false AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM updater.runs r WHERE r.plan_id = OLD.plan_id AND r.finished_at IS NULL) THEN
why: B2: a plan with a LIVE run may not be superseded, or a newer commit landing mid-update moves the plan out from under the run executing from it (review P2)
B3: `uncertain` must be able to reach the measured terminal states, or "Check and continue" cannot clear the state it exists to clear (review P1)

find:
IF OLD.state = 'uncertain' AND NEW.state IN ('succeeded','rolled_back')
      AND NEW.detail->>'measured' IS DISTINCT FROM 'true' THEN
why: B3: leaving `uncertain` as `succeeded` requires `detail.measured = true`, per design §11 — without it the database records a success on a run that admits it does not know what happened
B3: §9.7's attended hand-off must be able to record what the owner watched, or the attended upgrader cannot finish

find:
IF NOT p_terminal THEN
    INSERT INTO updater.run_events(run_id, ordinal, state, detail)
replace:
IF false THEN
    INSERT INTO updater.run_events(run_id, ordinal, state, detail)
why: B4: the journal mirror row is written by the SAME statement as the move; removing it leaves `guard_run_state`'s journal-agreement check to wedge the next step

find: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION updater.record_run_step(text, text, text, jsonb, boolean) FROM PUBLIC;
replace: -- mutation removes the revoke of the atomic transition function
why: B4: the web login owns the tables but must not reach the routine, or a compromised release can move a run row

find: IF NOT FOUND OR plan_kind IS DISTINCT FROM expected_kind THEN
why: M1: a rollback request must cite an approval for a `kind:rollback` plan; without the check it can cite an install plan's approval (review P5c)

find:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION updater.guard_owner_request_approval_kind() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path
replace:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION updater.guard_owner_request_approval_kind() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path
why: M1's kind guard must stay INVOKER: the web login already holds SELECT on updater.plans and on (id, plan_id) of plan_approvals — every column the body reads — so SECURITY DEFINER would be authority the guard does not need and the web does not have (measured)

find:
ALTER TABLE updater.owner_requests ADD CONSTRAINT owner_request_passkey_kinds
      CHECK ((request_kind IN ('rollback','serve_accepted')) = requires_passkey);
replace:
ALTER TABLE updater.owner_requests ADD CONSTRAINT owner_request_passkey_kinds
      CHECK (true);
why: M1: `requires_passkey` is derived from the request KIND, not chosen by the web login; without it a rollback can claim it needs no passkey (review P5a)
B4: repeating a step must be a no-op. Without it twenty concurrent callers asking for the same state each wrote a mirror event, so the run's journal carried twenty copies of one step
